channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Extends bearish spell below 111.50 as downside bias persists
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross trades in negative territory around 111.25 during the early European trading hours on Friday.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah holds losses as US Dollar receives support from Fed hike bets
item.description: USD/IDR inches lower after opening at a bullish gap, remaining in the positive territory and trading around 18,000 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair holds gains as the US Dollar (USD) finds support from growing expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Holds above mid-1.1300s amid Hormuz risks, bearish setup
item.description: The EUR/USD pair struggles to capitalize on the previous day's modest recovery gains and oscillates in a narrow band during the Asian session on Friday. Spot prices, however, hold above mid-1.1300s and the lowest level since May 2025, set on Thursday, warranting some caution for bearish traders.

item.title: Gold weakens back below $4,000 as Fed hike bets and Hormuz risks support safe-haven USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to capitalize on the previous day's modest recovery move and meets with a fresh supply during the Asian session on Friday amid the emergence of some US Dollar (USD) dip-buying.

item.title: Swiss Franc declines as Fed hike bets lift US Dollar
item.description: USD/CHF gains ground after registering nearly 0.30%, trading around 0.8100 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair rises as the US Dollar (USD) finds support from growing expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike.

item.title: Asian stock markets plummet as Apple price hike raises inflation concerns, KOSPI dives over 8%
item.description: Asian equity markets on Friday are significantly down as price hikes announced by Apple Inc. due to memory chip shortages have prompted fears of high inflation globally and concerns on earning projections of various companies that rely on these sophisticated chips for their final products.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar weakens below 0.5650 as Fed hike bets grow
item.description: The NZD/USD pair trades in negative territory for the eighth consecutive day near 0.5635 during the Asian trading hours on Friday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index advances on Fed rate hike bets
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, pares its recent losses from the previous day and is trading around 101.50 during the Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: British Pound bulls seem hesitant as Hormuz ship attack supports safe-haven USD
item.description: The GBP/USD pair sticks to a positive bias for the second straight day, albeit it remains below the previous day's swing high and trades just below the 1.3200 mark during the Asian session on Friday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains ground as oil prices rise
item.description: USD/CAD loses ground for the second consecutive day, trading around 1.4200 during the Asian hours on Friday. The pair depreciates as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) receives support from higher oil prices.

item.title: Australian Dollar edges lower to near 0.6900 on Fed hike bets
item.description: The AUD/USD pair edges lower to around 0.6900 during the Asian trading hours on Friday. The US Dollar (USD) strengthens against the Australian Dollar (AUD) on the expectation of US rate hikes later this year.

item.title: Japanese Yen consolidates near 40-year low vs USD after Tokyo CPI, amid intervention risks
item.description: The USD/JPY pair extends its sideways consolidative price move during the Asian session on Friday and currently trades just below the 162.00 mark, near a four-decade high.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.8166 vs. 6.8209 previous
item.description: On Friday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.8166 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.8209 and 6.8015 Reuters estimate.

item.title: WTI holds gains near $71.50 after cargo vessel hits near Oman
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gains ground for the second successive day, trading around $71.50 per barrel during the Asian hours on Friday.

item.title: Euro softens toward 13‑month low near 1.1350 as rising US PCE inflation lifts US Dollar
item.description: The EUR/USD pair loses ground to around 1.1365 during the early Asian trading hours on Friday. The major remains near a 13-month low as market expectations for US interest rate hikes have risen.

item.title: UN’s IMO pauses Strait of Hormuz evacuation plan after cargo ship attacked
item.description: The UN's International Maritime Organization (IMO) paused the planned evacuation of more than 11,000 sailors stranded in the Strait of Hormuz after a Singapore-flagged ship passing through the waterway was attacked, BBC reported on Friday.

item.title: Japan’s Tokyo CPI inflation rises in June: What 1.7% means for Japanese Yen
item.description: The headline Tokyo Consumer Price Index (CPI) for June rose 1.7% YoY as compared to 1.4% in the previous month, the Statistics Bureau of Japan showed on Friday.

item.title: Gold declines below $4,050 as US PCE inflation supports Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) declines to around $4,020 during the early Asian session on Friday. The precious metal extends the decline as traders have ramped up bets of a US rate hike. The Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index report is due later on Friday.

item.title: Crude Oil bounces on a Hormuz scare it doesn't believe
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) spent Thursday doing its now-familiar trick of grabbing a geopolitical bid and then quietly handing most of it back.

item.title: Mexican Peso rises as Banxico's hawkish hold fuels Peso rally
item.description: The Mexican Peso posted gains of over 0.62% against the US Dollar on Thursday after the Banco de Mexico (Banxico) unanimously decided to hold interest rates unchanged at 6.50%. The USD/MXN trades at 17.49, after reaching a one-and-a-half-month peak at 17.67.

item.title: Pound Sterling buckles in a leadership vacuum
item.description: Sterling spent the back half of June proving that a hawkish central bank counts for little when the government is falling apart.

item.title: Australian Dollar wins the data and still cannot rally
item.description: The Australian Dollar spent Thursday doing the one thing it was not supposed to do after a strong labour report, which is nothing.

item.title: Silver catches a bid, not a bottom
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) enjoyed a rare green session on Thursday, and reading much into it would be a mistake. The metal bounced off a session low near 56.35, briefly spiking close to 59.00 just after the US data hit the wires, before fading back to around 58.00, up roughly 0.8% on the day.

item.title: Firm data isn't hot enough for the US Dollar
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) had every excuse to extend on Thursday and declined instead. A firm batch of US data crossed the wires, yet the US Dollar eased off the top of its multi-month rally, slipping back toward 101.45 after probing close to 101.75 earlier in the session.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar eases after PCE data, Yen remains near intervention zone
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) lost momentum on Thursday, retreating toward the 101.40 area after a fresh batch of United States (US) economic data showed sticky inflation, stronger growth, and a resilient labor market.

item.title: Fed’s Williams: “Imperative” to return inflation to 2% target
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of New York President John Williams said in a speech released by text on Thursday that monetary policy remains “well positioned” for the current economy, while warning that inflation may take longer to return to the Fed’s 2% target than previously expected.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Weakness extends after breakout against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight a sharp USD/CNH spike to 6.8195, now seen consolidating between 6.8030 and 6.8185 on an intraday basis after an overdone rise.

item.title: Fed’s Goolsbee: “Inflation side of mandate is clearly the problem”
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday that inflation remains the central challenge for policymakers, warning that price pressure is still moving in the wrong direction despite some signs of improvement in services.

item.title: Banxico leaves interest rates unchanged at 6.50% as expected
item.description: The Bank of Mexico (Banxico) held its main reference rate unchanged at 6.50% in a unanimous decision on Thursday, as expected. Based on its economic projections, Banxico noted that the balance of inflation risks is tilted to the upside.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: US Dollar retreats below 0.8100 as ‘tweezer top’ forms
item.description: The USD/CHF pair stumbles on Thursday, losing 0.34% during the North American session, as the Greenback’s six-day rally stalls amid falling US Treasury yields, despite a red-hot US Core PCE inflation reading.
